explanation: Not on erdosproblems.com/1100; checked against [ErTe89], Théorème 1, (1.3): f(n) ≤ 3τ(n)·B_v^{ω_v(n)}, where ω_v(n) counts primes p with p^v ‖ n and the tabulated B_1 = 0.94494 = 3·2^{−5/3}. For squarefree n with ω(n) = k one has τ(n) = 2^k and ω_1(n) = k, so f(n) ≤ 3·(2·3·2^{−5/3})^k = 3·(3·2^{−2/3})^k. The Lean statement g k ≤ 3·(3/2^{2/3})^k for all k is exactly this specialisation (and gives the upper bound (2−c)^k since 3·2^{−2/3} ≈ 1.890). Correct.
